_about: Hand-checked interactions. 'a'/'b' are ingredient ids or 'class:<name>' (classes from ingredients.json). severity: avoid (don't combine without your doctor), caution (combine only if your doctor knows), timing (fine together but take apart; gap_hours used by the daily plan). Duplicate ingredients and duplicate drug classes are detected automatically.

interactions.effect: Ibuprofen and other anti-inflammatory painkillers can stop low-dose aspirin from protecting you, and together they raise the risk of bleeding.
interactions.advice: Use paracetamol for pain instead, unless your doctor says otherwise.
interactions.source: FDA science paper on ibuprofen and aspirin; ACOG

interactions.effect: Calcium reduces how much iron your body absorbs.
interactions.advice: Take them at least 2 hours apart.

interactions.effect: Antacids reduce iron absorption.
interactions.advice: Take iron at least 2 hours before or after an antacid.

interactions.effect: Acid-reducing medicines can lower iron absorption over time.
interactions.advice: Your doctor may check your iron levels.

interactions.effect: Iron binds thyroid medicine and stops it working fully.
interactions.advice: Take them at least 4 hours apart.

interactions.effect: Calcium stops thyroid medicine from being absorbed fully.
interactions.advice: Take them at least 4 hours apart.

interactions.effect: Antacids reduce absorption of thyroid medicine.
interactions.advice: Take them at least 4 hours apart.

interactions.effect: Magnesium reduces absorption of thyroid medicine.
interactions.advice: Take them at least 4 hours apart.

interactions.effect: Minerals reduce absorption of thyroid medicine.
interactions.advice: Take them at least 4 hours apart.

interactions.effect: Prenatal vitamins contain iron and calcium, which stop thyroid medicine being absorbed.
interactions.advice: Take them at least 4 hours apart.

interactions.effect: Acid-reducing medicines can slightly reduce thyroid medicine absorption.
interactions.advice: Your doctor may check your thyroid levels.

interactions.effect: Zinc and iron compete for absorption.
interactions.advice: Take them at least 2 hours apart.

interactions.effect: Iron blocks absorption of tetracycline antibiotics.
interactions.advice: Take them at least 3 hours apart.

interactions.effect: Calcium blocks absorption of tetracycline antibiotics.
interactions.advice: Take them at least 3 hours apart.

interactions.effect: Antacids block absorption of tetracycline antibiotics.
interactions.advice: Take them at least 3 hours apart.

interactions.effect: Iron blocks absorption of the antibiotic.
interactions.advice: Take the antibiotic 2 hours before or 6 hours after iron.

interactions.effect: Calcium blocks absorption of the antibiotic.
interactions.advice: Take the antibiotic 2 hours before or 6 hours after calcium.

interactions.effect: Antacids block absorption of the antibiotic.
interactions.advice: Take the antibiotic 2 hours before or 6 hours after an antacid.

interactions.effect: Iron reduces absorption of methyldopa, so blood pressure may rise.
interactions.advice: Take them at least 2 hours apart.

interactions.effect: Together they raise the risk of bleeding.
interactions.advice: Use paracetamol for pain instead, unless your doctor says otherwise.

interactions.effect: Together they raise the risk of bleeding.
interactions.advice: Sometimes prescribed together on purpose. Make sure the same doctor knows you take both.

interactions.effect: Together they greatly raise the risk of bleeding.
interactions.advice: Don't combine without your doctor's advice.

interactions.effect: Can cause serotonin syndrome and seizures.
interactions.advice: Don't combine without your doctor's advice.

interactions.effect: Small risk of serotonin syndrome.
interactions.advice: Tell your doctor you take both.

interactions.effect: Can cause serotonin syndrome.
interactions.advice: Don't combine.

interactions.effect: Can make epilepsy medicines work less well.
interactions.advice: Don't combine.

interactions.effect: Both can affect the heart rhythm (QT interval).
interactions.advice: Tell your doctor you take both, especially if you have heart problems or faint.

interactions.effect: Labetalol can make asthma worse and reduce how well the reliever inhaler works.
interactions.advice: Tell your doctor you have asthma.

interactions.effect: Beta-blockers can make asthma worse and reduce how well the reliever inhaler works.
interactions.advice: Tell your doctor you have asthma.

interactions.effect: Phenytoin and similar medicines lower folate levels, and folic acid can change their blood levels.
interactions.advice: Higher-dose folic acid is usually prescribed; your doctor will monitor levels.

interactions.effect: This medicine works against folate, which matters in early pregnancy.
interactions.advice: Make sure your doctor knows you are pregnant.

interactions.effect: Both cause drowsiness; together the effect is stronger.
interactions.advice: Avoid driving; ask your doctor if you need both.

interactions.effect: Together they cause more drowsiness and slower breathing.
interactions.advice: Ask your doctor if you need both.
interactions.source: FDA boxed warning (opioids with CNS depressants)

interactions.effect: Can make hormone treatments work less well.
interactions.advice: Tell your doctor you take both.

interactions.effect: Tea and coffee reduce iron absorption.
interactions.advice: Have tea or coffee at least 1 hour away from iron.

duplicate_classes.nsaid: Two anti-inflammatory painkillers together raise the risk of side effects without more benefit.
duplicate_classes.ppi: Two acid-reducing medicines of the same kind are rarely needed together.
duplicate_classes.h2_blocker: Two acid-reducing medicines of the same kind are rarely needed together.
duplicate_classes.ssri: Two antidepressants of the same kind can cause serotonin syndrome.
duplicate_classes.antiepileptic: Check that both epilepsy medicines are meant to be taken together.
duplicate_classes.raas: Two medicines acting on the same blood pressure pathway are not used together.
duplicate_classes.statin: Two cholesterol medicines of the same kind are not used together.
duplicate_classes.anticoagulant: Two blood thinners together greatly raise the risk of bleeding.
